ontology: driftwave_pin — locked invariants. The loop reads these; no agent, command, or artifact may retune them. Changing the pin is a human git commit, never a runtime act.
layer_tiers_note: The tier is derived from the layer, not trusted from self-report: L2/L3 are LLM judgment by construction, so dw_validate requires their artifacts to declare heuristic provenance and stamp not_acceptance regardless of what the producing agent wrote. L0/L1 are unmapped: L1 is the disclosed mixed case (computed record + LLM labels, see docs/HARNESS.md).
flag_vocabulary_note: flags[] is the ONLY sanctioned significance channel on an artifact. A flag not in this list is a validation failure, not a new feature. Every flag here has a real emitter (compute_persistence.py); a new flag is appended in the same human git commit that adds its emitter — pinning signals nothing can produce just makes readers reason about states that never occur.
prohibited_lexicon_note: Overclaim words may never appear in an artifact's claim-bearing fields (labels, reasons, findings). Enforced by dw_validate, not by good intentions.

state.never: /tmp — wiped on reboot, shared across projects; using it broke the cross-session memory claim (0.1.x)
